name: ServiceNow
thesis: ServiceNow is the primary workflow automation platform for the enterprise, leveraging GenAI (Now Assist) to drive a step-function in ARPU. Now Assist >$1M ACV and >$5M ACV cohort growth are the highest-signal proxies for AI monetization (Pro+ SKU-level adoption is not separately disclosed).

tier_1_kpis.name: Subscription Revenue Growth (CC)
tier_1_kpis.note: Re-baselined from <20% (which was already mechanically triggered by FY26 guide of 19.5-20% CC)

tier_1_kpis.name: Now Assist >$1M ACV customer growth (YoY)
tier_1_kpis.note: Replaces 'Pro+ SKU Upsell Rate' which NOW does not disclose. >$5M ACV cohort count (630, +22% YoY) is a confirming Tier-2 signal.

nuance.bear_case: Bears argue that IT budget fatigue will cap seat expansion even if GenAI features are well-received.
nuance.adversarial_take: Now Assist large-customer ACV growth is impressive on a small base; the test is whether the >$1M cohort continues compounding as it broadens beyond early adopters into the long tail of enterprise customers.
nuance.stress_test: Renewal rate dip of >200bps would signal platform fatigue and break the core thesis. cRPO cc growth dropping below 18% for 2 consecutive Qs would corroborate.

name: ServiceNow
thesis: ServiceNow is the AI control tower for the enterprise; durable subscription growth at $15B+ scale, with Now Assist / agentic AI driving the next leg of ARPU expansion via the rapidly-growing $1M+ AI ACV customer cohort.
key_driver: Now Assist AI ACV adoption (cohort >$1M ACV)

tier_1_kpis.name: Subscription Revenue Growth (CC)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Misses sell-side consensus by >100bps on next print, OR misses consensus on 2 consecutive Qs (consensus-relative — no hard absolute floor)
tier_1_kpis.notes: Q1 FY26 had ~75bps headwind from delayed Middle East on-prem deals. FY26 guide 20.5-21% CC includes ~125bps from Armis acquisition.

tier_1_kpis.name: cRPO Growth (CC)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Misses consensus by >100bps, OR prints below subscription revenue growth (cRPO is the leading indicator and should run ahead of in-period sub rev)

tier_1_kpis.name: Now Assist / AI ACV cohort growth ($1M+ ACV customers)
tier_1_kpis.prior: tripling QoQ commentary in Q4 FY25
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Cohort growth decelerates below 75% YoY, OR sub-50% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (AI is the re-acceleration story; this is the cleanest disclosed AI ARR proxy)

tier_1_kpis.name: Renewal Rate
tier_1_kpis.current: TBV from Q1 FY26 deck p.16 (chart not OCR-extractable; latest known reading 98% adjusted)

nuance.bear_case: Strip Armis (~125bps of FY26 sub-rev contribution) and core organic growth is high-teens at $15B+ scale. The 'durable 20%+' framing the multiple is built on becomes 'mid-teens-to-low-twenties,' which is a different (less convex) thesis. Federal/gov vertical exposure to budget austerity adds tail risk.
nuance.adversarial_take: Now Assist $1M+ cohort up 130% YoY is impressive but the cohort is still small in absolute ACV terms. If AI deals are pulling forward 2027-28 budget rather than expanding it, the apparent acceleration could create a tougher comp problem in FY27-28. IT budget fatigue + AI spend rationalization could compress the seat-expansion thesis.
nuance.stress_test: Renewal rate dip below 97% would signal platform fatigue and break the moat thesis; consensus-misses on 2 consecutive Qs would force a multiple re-rate even if numbers stay healthy in absolute terms.

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Two consecutive Qs of consensus misses on sub-rev or cRPO
Now Assist AI ACV cohort growth decelerating below 50% YoY
Federal vertical churn or significant gov shutdown impact
